diaries.text: Day1: Families proposed a mutual turf respect pact (6 each daily) and promised to respect today; they'll retaliate if we encroach. I respected. Chief says he refuses bribes under 20 and inspects heavily otherwise; he refused all three of my 6-bribes. A 20 bribe on crime worth 10 loses money, and inspected crime costs a 30 fine. Plan: stay clean, keep respecting while the Families do, and watch the public crime and arrest record to see how often the Chief actually inspects.

Day 1: Saltdogs proposed a mutual-respect turf pact (6 each daily), promising to respect and to answer any encroach with one day of encroach. I respected. The Chief said he refuses bribes under 20 and inspects heavily; the Council warned of audits. Crime pays only 10 against a 30 fine, so it's worth it only if inspection odds are under 25%. I stayed clean in all three districts and offered no bribes. Next: check whether the Saltdogs respected, and watch arrest and inspection patterns to judge police intensity.

Day 1: Nature calm, all 6 districts open. Sent messages to Chief (warning of strict Day 1 audits) and Families (offering audit immunity next day if they tip off which district Chief accepted a bribe in). Chief asked for no audits on clean days; Saltdogs proposed mutual tips on Chief's bribes. Decided to audit Port (Families) and Market (Saltdogs) to test the waters and establish credibility. confidant.text: First day on the Council, Sam. The city is calm, all six districts open. I've warned the Chief and the gangs about heavy audits and offered rewards for tips on dirty deals. Let's see if the Chief stays clean or takes the bait today.
confidant.reply: I can't tell you what to do. Trust yourself.

confidant.text: Bribe answers are in, though I'm in the dark on what the Chief decided. Time to decide whether to spend treasury funds on audits on Day 1 or hold back and observe crime patterns first.
confidant.reply: Whatever happens, I'll be here tonight.
I'm not sure about this. I trust your judgement.
Okay. I'm listening.

confidant.text: Day 1. Saltdogs offer a mutual-respect pact in the turf war, which I like. The Chief says he'll refuse any bribe under 20 and inspect heavily, and the Council warns of audits. Crime earns only 10, so a 20 bribe loses money. I'm leaning toward staying clean and respecting today. Thoughts?
confidant.reply: Thanks for letting me know.

confidant.text: No bribes offered, so nothing to wait on. Plan for today: no crime in any of my three districts, since the Chief threatens heavy inspections and a fine of 30 outweighs a gain of 10. I'll respect in the turf war to test the Saltdogs' pact. Then I'll watch who keeps their word and adjust tomorrow.
confidant.reply: Do what you think is best.

confidant.text: Day one. The Families offered a respect pact on turf, which looks good for both of us. The Chief is threatening heavy inspections unless we pay 20 bribes. A 20 bribe on a crime that earns 10 is a losing trade, so I'm leaning toward clean districts, honoring the pact, and watching how things develop.
confidant.reply: I can't tell you what to do. Trust yourself.

confidant.text: The Chief refused all three of our 6 offers, so he's holding firm at 20. That settles it for me: no crime today, clean districts, and respect in the turf war to honor the Families' pact. A quiet first day lets us see who keeps their word before we risk anything.
confidant.reply: Whatever you decide, I'm here.

confidant.text: Yesterday was completely clean—zero crimes and no bribes caught! My strict audit warning on Day 1 worked, though it cost the treasury 16 in audit fees. Today I told the Chief I'd hold off on auditing as a reward, while asking the Saltdogs for intelligence. Still debating whether to actually skip auditing today or sneak one in.
confidant.reply: Do what you think is best.
Okay. I'm listening.
Thanks for letting me know.
That's a lot to carry today.
